title: Lost Account Postmortem Pocket Guide
content:
Purpose: quick, repeatable pocket guide for running lightweight postmortems on lost accounts (won't replace the deep dive, but gives CS reps and EMs a fast path to surfaced insights for QBRs and renewal playbooks).

Scope: accounts lost after active engagement (demo -> pilot -> contract) where the customer explicitly chose another vendor, cancelled renewal, or halted implementation. Use this guide for: 30–60 minute triage, a 2–3 page summary for QBRs, and inputs into product/eng/ops feedback loops.

High-level flow (15–60m):
- Triage (10–20m): gather docs + stakeholder inboxes, quick timeline, top 3 suspected reasons.
- Evidence check (10–20m): label evidence strong/medium/weak, collect logs/Jira/conf tickets.
- Counterfactuals & mitigations (10–20m): list 2 realistic counterfactuals with owner and effort estimate.
- Outcome summary (5–10m): 1-paragraph contrarian summary + recommended next play (winback, docs, product fix, pricing change).

Role quick cheatsheet:
- AE: contract terms, price objections, decision-maker list, renewal posture.
- CSM: onboarding cadence, support tickets, enablement artifacts used.
- Solutions Eng / SE: POC success metrics, integration blockers, infra spikes.
- Product/Eng reviewer: technical root causes, bug/feature backlog items.

Minimum evidence checklist (mark Y/N):
- Contract and renewal date present? Y/N
- Decision-maker list captured? Y/N
- Last 30 days usage/telemetry snapshot attached? Y/N
- Support tickets timeline included? Y/N
- POC success criteria documented and measured? Y/N
- Pricing/discount history captured? Y/N

Loss reasons taxonomy (use this as labels — pick up to 3):
- Strategic shift: buyer deprioritized use case or changed stack.
- Price / economic: TCO too high, discounts insufficient, procurement constraints.
- Feature gap: missing critical capability, integration gap, API mismatch.
- Reliability / performance: latency, errors, data loss, quantization quality mismatch.
- UX / onboarding: activation friction, lack of enablement, slow time-to-value.
- Competitive: feature parity + packaged offering from competitor or incumbent.
- Compliance / security: regulatory or compliance blockers, KMS/HSM mismatch.
- People / org changes: buyer churn, reorg, budget holder left.

Template: one-page triage (fill during first call)
- Account: [company name]
- ARR lost: [number] (if available)
- Contract end / cancel date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- AE / CSM / SE owners: [names]
- Top 3 suspected reasons (short): 1) ___ 2) ___ 3) ___
- Evidence quick links: [ticket ids, confluence pages, demo video timecodes]
- Immediate next-step recommended: [winback email / product patch / refund / blocklist]

Timeline template (tick off events and attach links)
- Initial contact: [date] - notes link
- Demo/POC start: [date] - criteria doc link
- POC completion: [date] - telemetry snapshot link
- Contract signed: [date] - contract link
- Support incidents: [list dates/ids]
- Renewal negotiation start: [date]
- Cancel notice / competitor selection: [date] - reason stated by customer

Counterfactuals: (structured short form, required)
- CF #1: If we had shipped [specific feature/commitment] by [date], customer decision might have changed because [tangible reason]. Effort estimate: [3w / 2d / trivial]. Owner: [team/person].
- CF #2: If AE had pushed [procurement term or discount] or offered a pilot extension for free, potential delta = [ARR %]. Owner: [name].

Decision forks (what forced the final call):
- Fork A: Technical blocker (explicit): [short description]
- Fork B: Economic (explicit): [short description]
- Fork C: Time & org (implicit): [short description]

Synthesis guidance (for QBR slide): 3 bullets max that executives care about:
1) Root cause phrase, e.g., "Feature gap in streaming API caused POC failure"
2) Impact: ARR exposure and number of similar accounts (n=X)
3) Recommended action + owner + 30/60/90 day check-in

Playbooks by loss reason (concise actions):
- Strategic shift: classify into "recoverable" vs "abandoned". For recoverable: schedule strategy workshop and assign product champion.
- Price / economic: create an "economic relief" playbook: 30-day extended pilot, usage-based pricing trial, procurement template.
- Feature gap: run fast-track product triage: assign PM, estimate patch risk, create public ETA.
- Reliability / performance: escalate to SRE/serving-runtime + provide telemetry + prioritized hotfix.
- UX / onboarding: create personalized enablement, playbook to reduce TTV to <2 weeks, include SE office hours.
- Compliance / security: checklist for KMS/HSM + SOC2/ISO artifacts + engage security advocate.

Measurements & signals to feed back into ops:
- # of lost accounts by taxonomy per quarter
- ARR lost by taxonomy per quarter
- Median time from POC to cancel for lost accounts
- % of lost accounts with counterfactuals rated "highly plausible"

Follow-up timeline and owners (example):
- Day 0: postmortem triage doc created (owner: AE)
- Day 3: evidence packet and counterfactuals (owner: CSM)
- Day 7: synthesis slide + recommended playbook + handoff to PM/Eng (owner: Head of CS)
- Day 30: product decision / prioritization update (owner: PM)

Common pitfalls (avoid these):
- Too much blame, not enough evidence.
- Making the postmortem the only time product hears about the issue (we need a loop).
- Overly broad counterfactuals (must be specific and actionable).

Template language snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- "Customer cited integration gap with [system] as primary reason; telemetry shows X errors/min during POC window."
- "Counterfactual: shipping streaming-backpressure fix by [date] would likely have restored POC SLA; estimated 2wk effort."
- "Recommended play: offer a 90-day usage-based pilot plus SE office hours; owner: AE/CSM; check-in: 30 days."

Notes to self / scratchpad area (use during triage):
- Ask: did procurement docs actually block signature, or was it used as negotiation theater?
- Check PRs from demos: were code samples up-to-date?
- Slack threads with customer: grep for "concern" "capacity" "latency"
- Who on product leadership needs a 1-pager? Hint: 1-2 execs, not whole org.

Example one-paragraph postmortem (final blurb for QBR):
"Customer X ended renewal on 2025-01-15. Root cause: missing streaming API backpressure handling which caused repeated POC SLA misses and loss of stakeholder confidence. Secondary drivers: procurement friction and a competing vendor bundling integration. ARR exposure: $75k. Recommended immediate action: prioritize a small patch (PM owner: A. Gomez, 2-week ETA), and offer a 60-day usage-based pilot for re-engagement (owner: AE)."

Appendix: quick links to signal sources (attach in actual doc):
- Usage telemetry export (lookback 90d)
- Support ticket thread summary
- Demo recording timestamps (include exact minutes)
- Contract & SOW PDF

Open questions to resolve during triage (populate as you learn):
- Did any competitor feature ship during our POC window?
- Was there a single point person for procurement?
- Which other accounts share the same gap? (list candidate accounts)

Helper checklist for a 30m run:
- 0–5m: fill header (account, owners, ARR)
- 5–15m: gather and paste links (telemetry, tickets, contract)
- 15–25m: pick top 3 reasons + 2 counterfactuals
- 25–30m: write 3-bullet synthesis for QBR

End notes: keep this pocket guide intentionally short — use it to produce the one-pager that feeds QBRs and product triage. The deep-dive template should be used on larger accounts (> $250k ARR) or when legal/regulatory reasons are suspected.

-- Marina (CS lead) - iterative notes: add a reversible "winback leash" clause example for AE playbook, and a quick query to find peers in the tenant map.
